sections.h2: What does the Richmond County Register of Deeds handle for a seller?
sections.html:
The office records your deed so the sale to your buyer becomes part of the public record in Richmond County. It also records deeds of trust and plats, issues marriage licenses, keeps birth, death and marriage records, and gives oaths to notaries. The county seat is Rockingham, and the office is there.

Everything held by the office is public. Anyone may ask for copies by paying the posted fees, so a buyer, title examiner or neighbor can pull the same documents you can.

Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance is not good against lien creditors or buyers for value until it is registered in the county where the land sits, so the recording date counts.

sections.h2: Where and when can you record a deed in Rockingham?
sections.html:
The office is at 114 E. Franklin Street, Room 101, in Rockingham, and the same address serves as the mailing address. The county lists a phone line of 910-997-8250 for questions during business hours.

Walk-in hours and recording hours are not identical, and the difference is worth planning around. Electronic recording closes even earlier. Documents presented after 4:30 pm are recorded first thing on the next business day, according to the office FAQ.

Richmond County Register of Deeds hours as posted by the county

Because the cutoffs differ by service, call the office if you plan a late-day closing, and ask whether your attorney's firm submits electronically.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Richmond County?
sections.html:
The office FAQ quotes a $26.00 filing fee for a deed of up to 15 pages and $4.00 for every page beyond that. That matches the uniform schedule in G.S. 161-10.

  • A deed of trust or mortgage is $64.00 for 35 pages, then $4.00 per added page.
  • No fee applies to recording a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust.
  • Plats are $21.00 per sheet.
  • Certified copies are $5.00 for page one and $2.00 per added page.

For plain copies of a deed or plat, the office FAQ lists 35 cents per copy when you come in, and you may also mail a request. Give your name and the approximate year the property was acquired.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed excise tax on a Richmond County sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays. North Carolina sets the excise tax at $1.00 for each $500, or fraction of $500, of the price or value conveyed, and G.S. 105-228.30 says the transferor pays it to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.

The state statute then splits the money: one half goes to the county's general fund, the other half to the Department of Revenue after refunds and an allowance.

sections.h2: Can the Richmond County Register of Deeds help change names on a deed?
sections.html:
It can record the change, but it cannot draft it. The office FAQ tells owners who want to transfer or change names that a new deed has to be prepared, signed, notarized and then brought in for recording. It directs them to an attorney for the drafting.

Common situations where a new deed comes up before a sale:

  • A spouse is added or removed after a marriage or divorce.
  • An heir needs a name placed on title after a death.
  • An owner who holds property jointly wants to sell to a buyer alone.

If title questions pile up, your timeline slows. Sellers who want a faster path sometimes work with a direct buyer who will accept the property as it stands, but the recording rules above apply to every sale.

sections.h2: How can you search Richmond County land records and notary services?
sections.html:
The office FAQ confirms that no appointment is needed to take a notary oath, and that any staff member can administer it during regular office hours.

For a deed you signed years ago, search the online index first. If you want an image, you may come in and ask for a copy by name, or mail in the request. Plats can be requested as long as they were surveyed and recorded.

Your attorney will still run a title search and check for unpaid taxes before the deed goes in.

sections.h2: Which other papers get recorded in a Richmond County sale?
sections.html:
A deed is the main one, but not the only one. Under G.S. 47-18, a contract to convey, an option, a lease running longer than three years and a right of first refusal or first offer are all ineffective against lien creditors and buyers for value until registered in the county where the land lies. Priority follows the order and time of registration.

  • A seller-financed sale under a contract for deed must be recorded, or a memorandum of it recorded, within five business days under Chapter 47H.
  • A buyer's new mortgage appears as a deed of trust, priced at $64.00 for the first 35 pages.
  • A subdivision or boundary survey is recorded as a plat at $21.00 per sheet.

If you are not sure which of these applies to your sale, ask the closing attorney to list every document that will be filed.

sections.h2: What if the house in Richmond County is in foreclosure or an inherited estate?
sections.html:
Those paths run through the clerk of superior court, not the register of deeds. A power-of-sale foreclosure is heard by the clerk in the county where the land lies, with notice of the hearing served at least 10 days ahead under G.S. 45-21.16.

After a foreclosure sale is reported, anyone may file an upset bid within ten days. The new bid has to beat the last one by at least 5 percent, with a floor of $750, and each bid restarts the ten-day clock. Your sale is not final until that period runs out without a higher bid.

  • A small estate may use an affidavit when personal property after liens is $20,000 or less, filed with the clerk where the decedent lived.
  • The affidavit lists each tract of real estate the decedent owned.

Once a court or a seller has authority to convey, the deed itself still comes here for recording.

sections.h2: What should Richmond County sellers do before the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Ask the closing attorney for the recording date and for the satisfaction of your old mortgage. After closing, search the county index for both documents and keep the recorded copies.

Check your property tax status with the Richmond County tax office too. State law makes the lien for property tax attach on the January 1 listing date, so the year's bill follows the parcel until it is paid.

Finally, confirm how you will pay the excise tax and recording fee, since both are collected here before the deed is filed, and make sure the return address on the filing is one where you will actually get the recorded original. Keep the receipt for the fees, and compare the page count on the filing with the schedule above so the charge matches what you expected.

faqs.q: What are the Richmond County Register of Deeds recording hours?
faqs.a: In-person recording runs 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, and e-Recording runs 8 AM to 4:00 PM. The office is open until 5:00 PM, but papers presented after 4:30 are recorded first the next business day.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Richmond County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: It is 114 E. Franklin Street, Room 101, Rockingham, NC 28379, which is also the mailing address. The county lists 910-997-8250 as the phone number.

faqs.q: How much does a copy of a deed cost in Richmond County?
faqs.a: The office FAQ lists $.35 per copy when you get it in person. Certified copies follow the state schedule of $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each additional page.

faqs.q: Do I need an appointment to record a deed in Richmond County?
faqs.a: No appointment is mentioned for recording. Bring a signed, notarized deed during recording hours, or use e-Recording through an eligible submitter before 4:00 PM.

faqs.q: Can the register of deeds draft my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office says a new deed must be prepared by an attorney or by the owner, signed, notarized and then presented for recording.
